ports.intent: Read the current Gecko Node.documentGlobal API for Navis extension popup ownership and menu host detection.
invariants: Popup owner type, identity, transaction, source activity, privacy and view-type checks remain intact.
Tests model the pinned Node WebIDL surface rather than supplying the nonexistent ownerGlobal property.
ports.port_review: Review Node.webidl ChromeOnly global accessors and direct extension popup and context-menu host ownership.

ports.intent: Replay both valid popup Surface and widget bounds after native/compositor readiness, matching the ordinary render host.
invariants: Early Android layout cannot leave Gecko widget bounds unset when its compositor attaches later.
Released, failed, invalid and zero-size surfaces are not replayed; popup product identity and access checks do not change.
ports.port_review: Review Surface caching, compositor attachment, widget bounds and Android layout callback order.

ports.intent: Track popup screen geometry through Material sheet translation so accessibility bounds do not wait for the first touch to become correct.
invariants: Static frames do not send bounds JNI or resume the compositor; screen coordinates use the same convention as input correction.
Observer replacement, failed surfaces, release and detach cannot retain a stale geometry listener.
ports.port_review: Review screen geometry conventions, pre-draw observer lifetime and layout-only versus translated movement.

ports.intent: Let the ordinary DevTools menu restore Gecko's selected-panel preference while explicit Inspect continues to select the Inspector.
invariants: The private default sentinel maps to an omitted toolbox toolId; it cannot become an arbitrary tool identifier.
Gecko retains ownership of panel configuration and persistence; explicit inspection still requests Inspector.
ports.port_review: Review Android entry routing, nullable requested tools, private token validation and Gecko LAST_TOOL preference semantics.

ports.intent: Preserve Gecko's already resolved download filename through the native response and Java boundary for the platform download writer.
invariants: Gecko channel security and Content-Disposition precedence remain authoritative, including safe HTML download-name fallback.
The filename is separate metadata; no HTTP header is fabricated and no second network request is issued.
ports.port_review: Review channel filename resolution, JNI builder generation, response metadata lifetime and nullable adapter propagation.

ports.intent: Use the existing HTMLTooltip in-document path on Android, where a system principal does not imply a renderable native XUL popup widget.
invariants: All shared DevTools menus and tooltips use the same platform capability decision, not per-panel substitutes.
Desktop XUL wrapper behavior and non-system-document restrictions remain unchanged.
ports.port_review: Review Android widget popup rendering capability and HTMLTooltip focus, placement, dismissal and wrapper selection.

ports.intent: Offer a fixed private preference-flush operation so process relaunch can wait for Gecko's blocking preference-save path.
invariants: The save targets the active profile's explicit PrefF object; a null asynchronous save or timer cannot substitute for completion.
Only an acknowledged flush and unchanged live sessions allow the Android relaunch handoff; existing Gecko write-error semantics are not overstated.
ports.port_review: Review Preferences explicit-file blocking behavior, operation allowlist, save ordering and Android relaunch lifecycle validation.

ports.intent: Separate Gecko-confirmed text from optimistic Android IME edits, with ordered native replies and one input thread instead of replaying increments onto locally edited text.
invariants: Existing editable Binder methods remain the transport; no Console-specific character filtering or duplicate suppression is used.
Input connections are bound to their view and editor lifetime, and permanent Session closure clears text and pending actions.
Pre-IME dispatch does not swallow all keys and ACTION_MULTIPLE is expanded before reaching Gecko.
ports.port_review: Review GeckoEditable confirmed/shadow and ordered reply semantics, full resynchronization, selection ordering, composition and view/focus closure.

ports.intent: Expose bookmarks and topSites through the same Android product profile store, including committed bookmark events and strict permission-checked result delivery.
invariants: Product UI and extensions share one bookmark tree; errors are not replaced with successful empty data.
Permissions, extension/context lifetime and private access are checked before access and again before delivering asynchronous data.
topSites reads normal-history aggregates only; this does not claim history, sessions, search or find API parity.
ports.port_review: Review WebExtension schemas and event contracts, transaction commit ordering, shared-profile routing and permission/lifetime checks.

ports.intent: Normalize local accessible screen bounds to session client coordinates before the Android bridge applies the Surface offset once.
invariants: Remote accessible coordinates are unchanged; local coordinates and widget offsets are both layout device pixels.
No second CSS or zoom conversion is introduced and a missing widget is not dereferenced.
ports.port_review: Review local versus remote accessible Bounds contracts and Android Surface/client screen translations.

ports.intent: Give each Android framework input restart a distinct InputConnection so retiring the old connection cannot close the newly served editor.
invariants: Gecko-confirmed text and pending native replies stay with the Session, not the transient InputConnection.
Old connections cannot write or end a replacement connection's batch, and internal Unicode key fallback does not replace the IME connection.
ports.port_review: Review InputMethodManager create-new-then-deactivate-old ordering, connection ownership and stale batch closure.

ports.intent: Expose history through the same product store with real per-visit records, strict asynchronous results, committed events and normal-session-only ingestion.
invariants: Migration preserves known legacy aggregates without inventing historical visit IDs or timestamps.
New visit range deletion is exact; potentially overlapping legacy aggregates are removed conservatively rather than claiming unavailable per-visit precision.
Extension permissions and lifetime checks remain mandatory, and private navigation never produces persisted history.
ports.port_review: Review history schema/API event semantics, database migration and range deletion, navigation identity and private/late callback boundaries.

ports.intent: Receive remote browser page-title changes from the current WindowGlobal, with URI and navigation generation, including dynamic and restored documents.
invariants: Delayed events cannot update another document or a closed session, and native UI titles are not used as web history titles.
Private page titles update the live tab only and are not written into normal history.
ports.port_review: Review remote pagetitlechanged emission, WindowGlobal identity, location/STOP/BFCache ordering and Java-to-Core title ownership.

ports.intent: Connect file removal, file icons, system download-location actions and staged overwrite to the actual Android download store.
invariants: Destructive operations require exact owned or explicitly authorized files and the original extension/private-session authority.
Overwrite stages complete data first; provider replacement uses backup and rollback without claiming crash atomicity.
File-manager intent acceptance is not proof that a provider honored initial-folder positioning.
ports.port_review: Review download lifecycle and events, destination identity, Android file/document grants, staging cancellation and failed rollback recovery.

ports.intent: Use the live Navis search setting for extension search and reuse the pinned Gecko find actor/range implementation for accessible web documents.
invariants: Search and the omnibox share one provider catalog and URL policy; delayed operations retain their authorized target.
Find requires a current web presentation and document identity; native pages, private denial and stale results fail closed.
Per-browser find serialization protects the Gecko result cache; NEW_WINDOW uses the real windows backend and is not faked as NEW_TAB.
ports.port_review: Review search/find schemas, Gecko actor cache and frame traversal, context/permission lifetime, private tab ownership and mixed-presentation guards.

ports.intent: Bind native product pages and web entries to one real Gecko SessionHistory so back, forward and new branches retain the correct same-session presentation.
invariants: Traversal requires the actual entry identity and resolves only at the committed engine position; requested traversal is not completion.
Mixed metadata is validated against its engine snapshot and reanchored on restore; private history stays in memory.
Hidden native presentations cannot authorize extension find, late callbacks cannot steal navigation, and new branches do not retain discarded forward entries.
ports.port_review: Review Gecko SHEntry identity including child history, snapshot restore and traversal notifications, cancellation/timeout, branch replacement and native/web visibility ownership.

ports.intent: Expose the real product closed-tab store and restoration through the shared extension profile bridge, preserving verified engine and mixed-presentation history.
invariants: Normal HTTP(S) closed tabs only, bounded to 25; private tabs and window shutdown never enter the store.
POST history that cannot be serialized losslessly is not recorded as a misleading GET restoration.
Restore claims remain reserved until actual creation and durable consumption; failure retains the record and rolls back a partially restored tab.
Extension tab/window values are namespaced, closed-window restoration remains unsupported as on Desktop, and runtime window IDs are not persisted as stable identities.
ports.port_review: Review sessions schema, private access, value ownership, durable restore claims, engine snapshot capture and POST/subframe handling.

ports.intent: Project real product Activity/Core windows into extension APIs while retaining one Runtime and exact session, view, prompt and restore ownership.
invariants: Window creation, focus and removal resolve from real Activity, Core and topology acknowledgements, never from a new-tab substitute.
Privacy is window-scoped; extension tab lookup and action permissions use the source window, with real focus history and no private-window identifier leakage.
WebAuthn Activity leases are generation-bound and per window; old Activity destruction and late credential callbacks cannot replace or complete a new owner's request.
RestoreState is dispatched before HostReady reaches Platform, and recently-closed records are consumed only after actual restore-result and topology confirmation.
Android window geometry/state operations without an OS implementation explicitly reject instead of reporting fabricated success.
ports.port_review: Review Activity leases, window topology/MRU, private access and events, extension popup/action ownership, cancellation and asynchronous restore acknowledgements.

ports.intent: Route extension popup window.close through the owning direct Session and the existing Platform popup observer.
invariants: Only the current popup browser and its matching private window token may close that popup Session; normal content receives no popup close authority.
Popup-only allowscriptstoclose preserves Gecko closure semantics after popup navigation without changing the global script-close preference.
Late close callbacks cannot dismiss a replacement popup or another window; layout callbacks between close request and native acknowledgement do not access a closed Session.
ports.port_review: Review DOMWindowClose forwarding, popup token lifetime, frame-loader script-close permission, native acknowledgement and pending layout callbacks.

ports.intent: Host Gecko's original Responsive Design UI and actors on the existing Android page Session, alongside the independent in-app PAGE toolbox.
invariants: The browser container exists before first remote-browser insertion; responsive mode never replaces, copies or reloads the target document to provide a preview.
The PAGE toolbox retains the local-pipe remote-tab command path and persisted panel selection; no GeckoView Runtime owner, desktop docking lifecycle or remote debugging socket is introduced.
Only fixed viewport and close operations are exposed by the dedicated tools Session, with target ownership and matching privacy context enforced.
Normal exit waits for real ResponsiveUIManager cleanup, including an already-running toolbar close, and restores the entry zoom before releasing the tool host.
Failed initialization rolls back acquired frame, actor and viewport resources; native pages and removed Sessions cannot receive viewport commands.
ports.port_review: Review the current ESR's ResponsiveUIManager, tab events, browserContainer/browserStack CSS and actor destruction together. Revalidate the actual target viewport, original device toolbar, close races and unchanged page state on Android.

ports.intent: Confirm password saving only after the real Android Keystore/SQLite transaction commits, retaining a retryable original prompt on failure.
invariants: Engine-private candidates retain credential secrets; Platform prompt DTOs contain metadata and an opaque selection index only.
Actual Session privacy, request identity and callback ownership are checked before persistence; duplicate submissions and late results cannot resolve replacement prompts.
Storage exceptions, failed inserts and transaction commit failures propagate through the Java/Kotlin bridge; enqueue alone never reports success.
Gecko observers and native prompt completion follow commit, without issuing a duplicate storage write.
Closing a prompt withdraws presentation ownership, not a promise to undo an already accepted storage transaction. Document/POST association remains a separate required audit.
ports.port_review: Review LoginManager save/update producer semantics, immutable credential selection, private-session admission and completion/cancellation order through the Android storage transaction.

ports.intent: Make the original Gecko responsive toolbar and notification widget usable within the phone's owned page host without replacing its controls or emulation actors.
invariants: Narrow layouts retain original controls and handlers; observed real toolbar height reserves the matching space above the live page.
Only the owned system-principal Android RDM iframe can acquire temporary popup viewport space; hiding, destroying or failing a tooltip releases it.
DevTools alone leases the Android resize adjustment and one IME inset; leaving restores the previous adjustment without overwriting a newer owner.
Notification resources are scoped to the Android runtime; the real explanation, dismissal and explicit reload remain, with no automatic page reload.
The existing target Session, responsive actor cleanup and entry-zoom restoration remain unchanged; desktop presentation is untouched.
ports.port_review: Review responsive toolbar structure, popup measurement and lifecycle, NotificationBox assets and document changes together. Verify actual narrow-screen geometry, IME and actor state on device.

ports.intent: Bind delegated login selection and password-save authorization to the original remote document and real submission navigation instead of the long-lived chrome host.
invariants: Save tokens are parent-owned and browser-scoped; Java checks their authority before entering the retained commit transaction, never after writing credentials.
A normal form submission may survive its HTTP redirect using the replacement document channel's triggeringWindowId and isFormSubmission; URL similarity cannot grant that authority.
Same-document successful fetch/removal remains valid; unrelated navigation, native presentation, private saves, superseded prompts and foreign tokens are rejected.
Selections fill only through the captured WindowGlobal actor; old actor destruction or pagehide cannot cancel another document's new prompt.
HTTP authentication tokens originate only from the real AuthPrompter, not an arbitrary httpRealm value; existing challenge behaviour is retained without claiming new per-channel challenge validation.
Shared code enters the new host path only for Navis Android; desktop does not require a native source token or gain an Android lifecycle owner.
ports.port_review: Review actor lifetime and BFCache, form submission reasons, parent documentChannel redirect identity, native authorization ordering and exact prompt cancellation together. Preserve normal POST landing and same-document fetch behavior; validate real device integration separately from the method-level tests.

ports.intent: Connect desktop-aligned extension window presentation and bounds requests to the existing Android product Runtime and actual platform Task state.
invariants: Every asynchronous action rechecks the original extension/context, privacy access and source/target lease using an engine-owned bounded command token; CREATE reserves its new target before topology publication.
Window focus, minimization, browser immersive presentation and Task maximization are distinct facts, confirmed by actual Android state and Gecko topology rather than command admission.

API 34 Task mode changes carry trusted Gecko input qualification; system approval alone does not finish a mode transition. Confirmed same-Task restore ownership survives Activity recreation without reviving an old request lease.

Geometry uses public Android Task APIs, preserves existing Task/Session ownership, verifies only explicitly requested bounds fields and restores omitted focus state. Unsupported or ignored requests never report fabricated success.
Window attention obeys system notification authorization, private-safe text and exact live window ownership; it does not silently request permission or introduce an external debugging service.
Desktop behavior, the shared native engine ABI and GeckoView lifecycle ownership remain unchanged.
ports.port_review: Review extension call-context input metadata, event and topology conversion, command cancellation and private access together. Revalidate Android public Task APIs and observed mode/bounds acknowledgements separately from SDK type checks; never substitute View resizing or hidden APIs for Task behavior.

ports.intent: Let Android browser chrome read the current engine certificate identity without issuing or replacing a site-information sheet's authority to clear site data.
invariants: A site:get request with issueClearToken=false returns the existing authenticated identity and subject certificate while leaving the browser's clear-data token untouched.
Read-only results contain an empty navigationToken and canClearData=false; reading identity cannot grant or revive data-clearing authority.
Omitting the option or passing true preserves the existing sheet protocol; malformed option types are rejected before changing token state.
The current principal, document and WindowGlobal still govern site clearing; desktop behavior and the shared native engine ABI remain unchanged.
ports.port_review: Review the engine-owned securityUI and certificate projection together with siteRequests token lifetime. Verify repeated toolbar reads preserve an open sheet's token and do not revive tokens from a replaced document.

ports.intent: Synchronously relinquish an Android Session's compositor Surface before terminal state hides its live native owner and a replacement tab reuses the Surface.
invariants: Explicit Session close invokes the existing guarded synchronous surface pause before terminal cleanup and asynchronous native window destruction.
A shared Surface can move to the replacement tab without waiting for the old window's asynchronous close callback.
Nested finally blocks still attempt terminal cleanup and native close when surface pause or terminal callbacks throw; repeated close stays idempotent.
Unopened or compositor-detached Sessions do not call compositor JNI, and late compositor attachment cannot revive a closed Session.
The change is confined to the existing Android Java close method; native signatures, generated JNI declarations, shared engine ABI and desktop behavior remain unchanged.
ports.port_review: Review Java Surface ownership and compositor attachment guards together with synchronous native pause and asynchronous window close. Preserve exception cleanup and test actual-device rendering after closing the active tab; method-level ownership tests do not establish GPU output.

ports.intent: Expose the same engine certificate details and authenticated built-in extension distinction used by the desktop site-information presentation.
invariants: Certificate display names, public-key digest, key exchange and signature are read from the existing engine security objects, never web content.
Certificate chains use the handshake fallback only when the succeeded chain is empty, remain bounded to sixteen entries and exclude missing certificates.
Only an authenticated active extension listed by the immutable application-built-ins preference receives builtInExtension=true; user extensions are not labeled application-owned.
Certificate errors retain priority over loopback identity; read-only queries and clearing-token principal/document/WindowGlobal checks are unchanged.
No JNI, native engine ABI, network service or desktop product behavior changes.
ports.port_review: Compare DesktopEngine projectCertificate/projectSecurityDetails and applicationBuiltInIds with the current engine security getters. Preserve bounded read-only projection and authenticated extension ownership.

ports.intent: Reuse the desktop process manager, local diagnostics and packaged license reader behind the fixed Android product operation table.
invariants: Only the native product host can issue these operations; no script evaluation or arbitrary preferences are exposed.
Process termination uses short-lived tokens, revalidates PID and child identity, and protects the current host process.
Diagnostics report actual retained runtime facts; license text comes from the packaged resource without network access.
Desktop and Android consume the same service implementation without JNI or native engine ABI changes.
ports.port_review: Review the fixed product dispatch table and shared DesktopProductPages module when updating upstream process info or packaged license resources.

ports.intent: Allow Navis to select a distinct Android child service class namespace before each profile parent starts Gecko, so concurrent profiles never share fixed socket, GPU, RDD, utility or ordinary content service instances.
invariants: Without product configuration Gecko retains the original GeckoChildProcessServices namespace.
Service class selection freezes on configuration or first lookup; an active parent cannot change child namespaces.
The existing allocator, isolated instance UUIDs, service flags and native JNI signatures remain unchanged.
Navis Gradle generates each profile namespace and distinct Android process names from the pinned service manifest, preserving isolatedProcess and useAppZygote attributes.

Extension notification receivers run in their owning profile process; system tags and PendingIntent identities include a fresh parent-process UUID, preventing cross-profile overwrites and stale clicks after slot reuse.
ports.port_review: Review service component naming, manifest service-count/flag queries and child ownership checks together. Keep every default and isolated child service in the selected profile namespace and verify two profile parents concurrently before package acceptance.

ports.intent: Permit the existing desktop settings document to change between its five canonical navis://settings routes through History API without a page reload.
invariants: The additional path-rewrite branch compiles only when the desktop internal scheme is configured and Android is not targeted.
Both source and target must have the settings host, no credentials, no explicit port, no query and a known settings route.
The original scheme, same-origin and userpass checks remain mandatory; other internal hosts and unknown paths gain no rewrite permission.
Normal web, extension and existing fragment-only History API semantics are unchanged.
ports.port_review: Review Document::CanRewriteURL scheme and same-origin guards together with DesktopInternalPages settings route definitions. Verify actual packaged pushState/popstate, document identity preservation and rejected cross-host/unknown-route targets; mock History API tests alone are insufficient.

ports.intent: Connect Android's startup and live appearance requests to the shared desktop appearance preference policy instead of rejecting the initialization chain as an unknown operation.
invariants: The native host allowlist adds only appearance:set; unknown operations and invalid payload guards remain enforced.
Appearance requests contain exactly an own key and string value; only theme and accent are exposed, not arbitrary preferences or desktop-only settings.
The shared policy validates system/light/dark and six-digit RGB colours and applies the same content colour-scheme and system-theme preference semantics on both platforms.
The Android package explicitly installs the shared NavisSettingsPolicy module; this change adds no native code or runtime ABI.
ports.port_review: Review AndroidProductServices initialize/setAppearance, host PRODUCT_QUERIES, Android product dispatch and the shared module installation as one end-to-end contract. Exercise the actual JS dispatch with valid startup requests and rejected arbitrary keys/invalid values, then verify the packaged bytes before device acceptance.

ports.intent: Make Restart with Add-ons Disabled suspend Navis user-facing registered built-in and temporary extensions instead of inheriting Gecko's internal built-in safe-mode exemption.
invariants: Only Navis Core products change behavior; unmodified Gecko retains its original policy.
The exact product-owned applicationBuiltins allowlist and extension type identify user-facing built-ins on Desktop and Android despite their different installation locations.
Locale packages and non-product system/runtime add-ons retain upstream exemptions, preserving Android locale initialization and required engine components.
Both fresh policy computation and the BootstrapScope getter reject affected extensions, even when an existing profile caches runInSafeMode=true.
Safe mode does not alter userDisabled or product extension preferences; a normal restart restores the user's previous enabled state without native code changes.
ports.port_review: Review canRunInSafeMode, XPIState startup caching and BootstrapScope together. Confirm real Services.appinfo.inSafeMode and extension isActive across normal-to-safe-to-normal process restarts using an existing cached profile, while retaining locale and system components. Android installBuiltinAddon uses a different location from Desktop's restricted application directory and must remain covered.

ports.intent: Include the Android color-picker library attribution and complete license in the Android module graph actually traversed by the runtime build.
invariants: Only the Navis Android runtime adds the library notice; desktop packaging does not claim the Android UI dependency.
The packaged modules/navis-licenses path matches the fixed resource URI in the shared offline credits reader.
The application-owned notice preserves the unmodified pinned upstream Apache 2.0 license and attribution.
This resource declaration does not change native code, JNI, extension policy or the Kotlin/Compose toolchain.
ports.port_review: Review the Android mobile/shared/modules/navis graph, not the untraversed desktop module graph. Verify the final APK assets/omni.ja contains the exact modules/navis-licenses/colorpicker-compose-1.1.4.txt bytes and that shared credits can read it offline.

ports.intent: Restore Gecko SearchService, engine models, SearchSettings and anonymous suggestion controller behind a single Profile-owned Navis offline search policy.
invariants: The fixed four seeds and existing custom or edited providers preserve stable IDs, names, templates, order and defaults through one-time migration.
Mozilla remote search configuration, eager remote icons, region/experiment policy and search telemetry do not activate under MOZ_NAVIS_CORE.
Navis search does not depend on Places or FormHistory; platform records enter only the bounded local suggestion contract.

Remote suggestions require durable opt-in and reject private contexts, addresses and paths before transport; cancellation prevents stale results. Navis Profile consent is the sole product gate, independent of GeckoView's disabled-by-default legacy suggestion preference.
Gecko-owned persistence is awaited and failures preserve acknowledged state; non-Navis upstream behavior remains unchanged.
ports.port_review: Re-inventory eager selector/configuration initializers, SearchSettings atomic persistence, UserSearchEngine mutation/submission and suggestion transport/cancellation. Review Android registration and all existing consumers against each target ESR.

ports.intent: Route Android search configuration, submissions, suggestions and extension search through the shared Gecko search service with one-time Profile migration.
invariants: Android settings cache Core projections and never write a parallel search configuration.
Private Sessions never issue remote suggestions; opt-in, query classification, cancellation and stale-document guards stay inside Core.
Local bookmark/history/tab candidates remain bounded Profile values; private history and foreign-mode tabs are excluded.
Live extension catalogue and named/default submissions use Gecko without new extension permissions.
Only product:initialize accepts a 512KiB legacy payload; ordinary operations retain 64KiB bounds.
ports.port_review: Review Gecko search initialization, engine metadata/submission/controller APIs, Android host query bounds and extension privacy/navigation guards against the target ESR.

ports.intent: Apply the current Navis accent to normal default selected text while retaining author and system selection semantics.
invariants: The fallback is limited to MOZ_NAVIS_CORE; authored foreground or background selection styles retain priority.
Attention, disabled and IME selection states retain upstream colors.
Forced document colors, OS accessibility themes, always-high-contrast and existing Highlight stand-ins bypass the product fallback.
No global ui.highlight or CSS system Highlight override is introduced.
A fixed accent default permits ordinary preference propagation, while existing style-change notifications repaint live windows.
ports.port_review: Review nsTextPaintStyle normal-selection fallback and contrast correction, color notification/pref propagation and platform accessibility/stand-in guards. Require native paint verification after each engine update.

ports.intent: Retain Gecko's complete safe download-launch path in embedders without the optional enterprise-policy service.
invariants: An absent policy service grants no executable-confirmation exemption.
Present enterprise policies retain their domain and extension exemption decision.
Executable consent, Windows security-zone behavior, MIME/system handlers and the extensionless Windows safeguard remain unchanged.
Neither shell commands nor a direct nsIFile launch bypass replaces Download.launch.
ports.port_review: Review DownloadIntegration.launchDownload optional enterprise-policy lookup and the surrounding executable/MIME checks. Retain only the absent-service guard if the target ESR still assumes enterprise policies exist.

ports.intent: Keep Navis names and artwork owned by the product when a signed Mozilla language pack supplies all ordinary translated Gecko strings.
invariants: The pinned Mozilla language-pack archive and its signature remain byte-for-byte unchanged.
Only branding/brand.ftl, toolkit/branding/brandings.ftl and the legacy branding locale alias fall back to application-owned resources; ordinary translated strings still come from the language pack.
The override is selected by MOZ_NAVIS_CORE and shared by desktop and Android rather than duplicated in platform UI.
The exact-index Fluent source uses the language pack's existing metasource, is registered after translated sources, and is removed with the language pack.
Android legacy and standard branding image names resolve to the canonical product/branding generated assets without changing native configuration or libraries.
Non-Navis Gecko products retain their original branding and language-pack behavior.
ports.port_review: Review language-pack chrome registration, L10nRegistry metasource ordering and Android branding jar paths together. Verify en-US and zh-CN product names, Navis Profiler, unchanged signed XPI bytes, content-process propagation and every packaged image alias on each target ESR.
